description: Abandon a running move instance (instance, plus session naming the session it belongs to). Or tear down a session directly by handle (session alone): one call, no resume, no framing. The response names the label and discarded threads. Nothing is cleaned up implicitly: held WIP markers are surfaced and left standing for resume or grooming. The session shell concludes through its own junction, never through abandon.

held.description: for each served piece whose text you still see: its tag and the word right after the tag, as tag:word (e.g. "… dialogue ⟦gn9p⟧ first …" → gn9p:first). A proved piece serves as a short pointer; never guess a word

instance.description: instance handle of the move to abandon; pass session too, naming the session the move belongs to

reason.description: why the instance or session is being abandoned

reread.description: tags or piece names of served pieces you no longer see; they serve in full again

session.description: with instance: the attached session the move belongs to (required). Alone: a session handle to tear down directly; no resume, no framing

name: abandon

description: Declare or clear the attached session's durable branch binding. Pass exactly one of branch or clear:true. Setting validates the live registered checkout before changing the session; clearing needs no branch capability.

name: bind_branch

description: Ground a draft before its capture, in one call; session required. On a small graph: every live entry's brief. Above it: a semantic search, keyword searches and the live listing of every draft topic, written from the draft. Name the running capture as instance: only reads made through gather inside it ground the capture. Pass ids to open entries in full. An entry the call proves it holds prints as a pointer with its brief.

draft.description: without instance: the draft text the searches are written from; credits nothing

description: Advance a procedure instance; session required. Send state fields per the served report_schema, or answer a pending chooser with {chooser, choice, userWords?, reason?, fields?}. User choosers must carry the user's answer, relayed verbatim, in userWords. Exception: the served schema offers reason for a choice you decide yourself. Unfinished operation: omit report and pass its exact retry_ref to continue, or cancel_ref to leave its effects in place and return to the preceding interaction. Other transitions stay blocked until the operation is retried or cancelled. When a move ends, the response carries the session shell's serve: where the dialogue lands.

cancel_ref.description: exact cancellation reference from a failed operation; leaves effects in place and returns to the preceding interaction; mutually exclusive with report and retry_ref

retry_ref.description: exact retry reference from a failed operation; mutually exclusive with report and cancel_ref

session.description: attached session's handle, from start_session or resume_session; required. Retain it across context compaction

Use it when the user shelves work mid-dialogue. A seeded draft then parks as a graph-visible thread, not as an agent promise living in conversation memory.

name: registry

description: The second door, and the compaction escape. Re-serves the current position of the session whose handle you present: its framing plus every running move at its current step, each with the report schema to continue it. Presenting the handle is the whole authorization. A handle reaches you only by issuance or by the user handing it over. Presenting it also declares you need re-serving: every piece of the position serves in full. Only recorded session state resumes (step position, collected fields, staged files), never another conversation's context. A lost handle is the user's to recover, not yours to guess.

session.description: session handle (the session ID) whose current position to re-serve: its framing plus every running move at its current step, with the schema to continue it. Presenting the handle is the whole authorization. It also declares you need re-serving: every piece of the position serves in full, whatever the call holds

description: Stage a file into the session scratch; session required. Returns a handle and the sha256 of the staged bytes. Pass the handle in a report's attachments field, or as a capture's bodyHandle when the file holds the entry body. Or amend what is already staged: with patches, the file named by name is edited in place through atomic search-replace pairs, not re-staged whole. A path is only read, never written. Never a graph write: the write gate materializes staged files with the entry.

patches.description: edit the already-staged file named by name in place: ordered exact search-replace pairs, applied atomically. Each old must match exactly once; a failing pair refuses the whole edit. Pass instead of content/path

new.description: replacement text; empty deletes the old text

old.description: exact text to replace; must match exactly once in the file as it stands when this pair applies

path.description: local file path to stage instead of inline content

description: Open a fresh dialogue session. One of the two doors, and the only tool that takes a project. Auto-starts the session shell (user-dialogue by default). Returns its opening serve: your orientation, the available moves, and the session handle. The handle is the dialogue's identity and binds the session to one project. Retain it across context compaction. Pass it to every other tool, reads included. Pass project when the composition serves several. Without project, a sole accessible project is inferred. With several, the response lists them (status project-required) and opens no session. Every call opens a new dialogue under a new handle. To re-serve an existing one, present its handle to resume_session.
